> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (symbol, 39 pages)`, `created_at (literal, 39 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49b505915a37270ddf12d0ed4a6fd67f9907fb74` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c5a88d1e4d0ed32fb211671f1fbbd3b3199c7e38` — the merge of head `b97005bf14417759f5fdf57e4cb90c41622774bd` into base `49b505915a37270ddf12d0ed4a6fd67f9907fb74`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c5a88d1e4d0ed32fb211671f1fbbd3b3199c7e38 && git checkout c5a88d1e4d0ed32fb211671f1fbbd3b3199c7e38
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 49b505915a37270ddf12d0ed4a6fd67f9907fb74 b97005bf14417759f5fdf57e4cb90c41622774bd && git checkout -B drift-repro 49b505915a37270ddf12d0ed4a6fd67f9907fb74 && git merge --no-ff b97005bf14417759f5fdf57e4cb90c41622774bd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 49b505915a37270ddf12d0ed4a6fd67f9907fb74
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 49b505915a37270ddf12d0ed4a6fd67f9907fb74` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4efa377e203fb1b515195033c56e57c104b90739`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-route.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-route.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/flow-route.integration.test.ts, ui/apps/console/src/services/approvalsApi.ts, ui/apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.servedPageStepLine-12491.test.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/README.md, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useRecordApprovals.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordApprovalsPanel.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordApprovalsPanel.servedRoute-26668.test.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordApprovalsPanel.stepProgressVertical.test.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordApprovalsPanel.visitedRoute-26563.test.tsx (deleted), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/approval-decision/ApprovalDecisionPanel.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/approval-decision/ApprovalDecisionPanel.stepLine-12491.test.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/approval-progress/ApprovalStepLine.tsx; cited code read on `origin/main` `7bb80845`: packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts (`traverseNext`), packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts (`FlowNodeAction`, the edge schema), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.ts (resume labels, auto-approve), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts (`formatOutput` datetime canon), the pre-change `attachFlowSteps`. Prose faces (`.changeset/26668-approval-served-route.md`, `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`) are the dispatching seat's ACCEPT, not this record.

Inputs: card #26668 (body; comments 6442524346, 6445757080, 6446765160, 6455118705, 6456589397), card #26563 and PR #26666 (body, files), PR #26976 (body, 18 files, the one comment 6456593091, the net diff against main at the head), the head's check-runs. Read-only throughout; no worktree, build, test or gate run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set / public face.** `ApprovalRequestRow` (`@objectstack/spec/contracts`) gains one optional served member `flow_route?: { steps, ahead: 'end' | 'undecided' | 'decided' }`; `flow_steps` is byte-identical in shape and producer, its doc rewritten to say it is the trunk and that a step line draws `flow_route`, never it. Widening of a published read contract; nothing an author writes moves. Correct as declared.

2. **⛔ No guessed path — judged on the producer (`approval-route.ts`, `attachFlowRoute`).**
   - Passed steps come ONLY from the run's own `sys_approval_request` rows: the service reads `where: { flow_run_id: row.flow_run_id }` as the system, and `passedSteps` keeps a row only if it is another node, `approved`, opened before the request (`created_at` compare) and, per node, its latest round. The current step is `row.flow_node_id`. The graph is never consulted for either. Correct.
   - Steps ahead (`stepsAhead`): from an approval node the `approve`-labelled out-edges, else every non-fault out-edge — exactly the engine's rule in `traverseNext` (claim by `branchLabel`, else every out-edge, `fault` excluded). It follows ONE edge with no `condition` and returns `undecided` at a `decision` node (even with one edge), a conditioned edge, more than one out-edge, a node already seen, a node not in the graph, or a `subflow` / `map` / `loop` / any node with `regions`. A single `isDefault` edge is followed, which is what the engine does when no conditional sibling exists. The trunk is never substituted: nothing in the module reads the `true` edge or `out[0]`. Correct.
   - Shapes probed, with what `ahead` says: a re-entered step (loop back) stops at the seen node, `undecided`, after listing the steps up to it; a rejected-then-resubmitted run (ADR-0044) lists no `returned` / `rejected` row, lists a re-approved node once at its latest round, and never walks the `revise` / `reject` edges because the node's `approve` edges exist; a parallel or fan-out (`parallel_gateway`, or any node with two unconditioned out-edges) stops `undecided` — two pending requests of one run each see the other's approved rows as `done`, which are facts of the run; a run with no history rows yields passed `[]` and the walk alone; a request with no `flow_run_id` or no `flow_node_id` gets no `flow_route` (documented); a flow edited after the request started is read at its current version — the request's own node missing from the graph gives `{ steps: [passed, own], ahead: 'undecided' }`, a passed node missing is labelled from the stored `current_step_label`, a deleted flow gives no `flow_route` at all (no guess, a gap); a non-pending request (approved, rejected, returned, cancelled, recalled) is passed + own (`done` once approved, else `current`) with `ahead: 'decided'` and no walk.
   - `decided` is served only when `row.status !== 'pending'`, and then never with a walked tail. Never served without a decided path.
   - Not a guess but an omission, noted for the record: an auto-approved rung (#3447, empty slate, no request row) is absent from the passed steps.

3. **Two fields.** Readers of the rail now read ONLY `flow_route.steps`: `RecordApprovalsPanel` (`pendingRequest?.flow_route?.steps`, the pending request being the one row the hook enriches by `getRequest`, so the single-read member reaches it), `ApprovalDecisionPanel` (`request.flow_route?.steps`, at any status), and `ApprovalStepLine`'s step type is now `flow_route`'s. The two type declarations (`ApprovalRequestLite` in app-shell, the console's `approvalsApi.ts` row) carry both members, each doc saying the line draws `flow_route` and nothing draws `flow_steps`; the app-shell README and the approvals guide say the same; the spec doc on `flow_steps` says it. `git grep` on `origin/main` finds no other reader: no `packages/client` type, no OpenAPI or `content/docs/references` output names `flow_steps` (the only other hit is a liveness-evidence string naming `attachFlowSteps`, whose producer is unchanged). Nowhere do the two fields disagree without the doc saying which the UI reads. The spec doc's stop list omits the two extra conservative stops the code has (missing node, `regions`); the guide's matches the spec. Not a disagreement.

4. **Declarations.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — right (one added optional member of a published contract). `Metadata-protocol: none` — right: the rule (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3) grades the change to what a metadata author can write; `flow_route` is a served read member, no key, value or type an author writes moves. The claim's `added` was marked provisional and assumed an authorable key; the dev's re-judgment from the diff stands. Precedent #26361 holds: it added the optional `getRecordLock?` member to `IApprovalService` in the same contract file under `yes (widening)` / `none`. `Skills-docs: none` — the third line is not owed at all (kind `none`, arm `widening`); `git grep` over `skills/` for `flow_steps`, `flow_route`, the step line or progress strip: 0 hits, so the guide's new paragraph makes no skill text false. `ADR-0087:` no marker owed — no breaking changeset (no `!`, no `(narrowing)`, patch everywhere), and the gate reads the breaking declaration alone. Changesets: one entry per touched published package (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/console`), all `patch`, each body carrying both declaration lines.

5. **Stopgap deletion (#26666).** `visitedApprovalSteps` and the request page's no-line rule are deleted; `ApprovalStepLine`'s markup is untouched. Tests, one by one: `RecordApprovalsPanel.visitedRoute-26563.test.tsx` **removed** with its subject — its four panel pins are **re-pinned** in `RecordApprovalsPanel.servedRoute-26668.test.tsx` (the reported route with no trunk rung; a one-step route draws none; the viewer served only the pending row now sees the whole route, inverted on purpose because the route no longer comes from the list read; the rejoin-trunk case moved to the server where the rule now lives, integration case 3), its seven unit pins on the deleted function are **re-pinned** as `passedSteps` cases in `approval-route.test.ts` (order, outcomes that are not a pass, later rows, the current node's earlier rounds, round dedup, missing node or time); `RecordApprovalsPanel.stepProgressVertical.test.tsx` **re-pinned** to served-route fixtures, its connector-tint case now pinning both tints (green into done/current, `bg-border` into upcoming) where it pinned all-green under the no-ahead regime; `ApprovalDecisionPanel.stepLine-12491.test.tsx` **re-pinned** from "no line" to the drawn route, adding no-route-draws-nothing and line-above-tally-above-decisions, the old tally control kept inside the ordering case; the console `servedPageStepLine-12491` (the real served page) **re-pinned** likewise, its `queryByRole('list')` null-check dropped because a list now legitimately exists. No retained assertion is weakened. A trunk request renders the same for every reader: integration case 5 pins `flow_route.steps` deep-equal to `flow_steps` at every step of a linear flow with `ahead: 'end'`, and both panels draw one `ApprovalStepLine` from that one member.

6. **Tests pin the real service path.** `flow-route.integration.test.ts` boots a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver`, the real `AutomationEngine` with its logic nodes (the gateway is a real `decision`), the real approval node and `ApprovalService`; every request is opened by the engine and every decision resumes the run; the route is read through `svc.getRequest`. The dev's repro on `origin/main`'s producer reports 5 of 6 red: the green one is case 6, "the list read serves no route, as it serves no `flow_steps`" — green on both sides by construction (the list read never served either member), which is what the dev reports; case 1's `flow_steps` assertion is likewise green on both sides on purpose. The unit file covers the branch kinds a live run reaches slowly.

7. **Gates.** The dev's 110 locally derived gates are the dev's reading and do not carry to the head; the head's check-runs are the verdict. Readings of `/commits/4efa377e…/check-runs`: at 2026-10-27T23:57Z 40 runs, 29 in progress, 0 failures; at 2026-10-28T00:05Z 60 runs, 28 in progress (the 16 Test UI shards, 8 Test Core shards, Lint UI, Type Check UI, two Type Check lanes), 26 success, 6 skipped, 0 failures. Final reading before this record was written, at 2026-10-28T00:09Z: 61 runs, 41 success, 6 skipped, 0 failure, 14 still in progress (Test UI shards 2, 7, 8, 9, 12 and 14 of 16; Test Core shards 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 of 8; Lint UI; Type Check UI). An in-progress gate is an honest reading, not a pass: no check on the head has failed, and the landing pre-check (every check green) is the owning seat's to re-read before the queue; this record does not stand in for it.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on all four touched published packages. Right by the rule: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` whatever its Clause-② arm. No `minor` is owed because no authorable surface moved; no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 disposition, no tombstone. Changeset bodies and the PR body carry the same two declaration lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, "the line does not mark an undecided tail": accepted. The served row says `ahead: 'undecided'`; the line ending at the last listed step draws no guess. A marker is a ui follow-up if wanted, not a defect.
- Dev flag, "who sees which steps changed on the record panel" (the run's rows are read as the system): accepted. What crosses is step ids, labels and states, which `flow_steps` already served to the same reader; no approver, payload or comment data rides it.
- Dev flag, ordering by `created_at` with a same-millisecond tie: accepted; a run opens its next request only after the previous decision. `created_at` is written as an ISO string and `formatOutput` canonicalises `Field.datetime` to ISO on read on every SQL dialect, so the rule's `typeof === 'string'` guard holds off sqlite too.
- Dev flag, the full `packages/app-shell` suite not run locally: the 16 `Test UI` shards on the head are the reading (see ① 7).
- Deviation, `Metadata-protocol` re-judged from the claim's provisional `added` to `none`: the re-judgment is right (① 4).
- Deviation, branch `claude/project-thread-04q6o5` rather than `claude/issue-26668-*`: platform-assigned, written as measured in the claim; `Implemented-by` names it.
- Observation, non-blocking: `stepsAhead` seeds `seen` with the current node only, so a walk that re-enters a step already in `passedSteps` would list that id twice and `ApprovalStepLine` keys rows by `s.id`. Reachable only on an unconditioned `approve`-edge cycle, which the engine would itself loop on; no guess is drawn. A follow-up may seed `seen` with the passed ids.
- Observation, non-blocking: the `passedSteps` docblock says rows of other runs are ignored; the function does not filter by run — the caller's `where: { flow_run_id }` does. Doc nit.
- Observation: `attachFlowRoute` adds one system read per single get (`limit: 1000`), display-only and caught, as `attachFlowSteps` is.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay login to name.
- Governed surfaces: none of the 18 paths; 1,544 changed lines, under the 3,000 threshold; not Tier H. The schema face alone makes this review owed. Landing stays the owning seat's, through the queue, once every check on the head is green.
